A0029.title: Data Profiling
A0029.definition: Abstracting multi-source data such as users, devices, and IPs into a tagged model, using clustering, classification, and statistical baseline comparison to identify entity risk and anomalous deviations.
A0029.description: Data profiling collects multi-dimensional data such as user attributes, device information, and behavioral traces, abstracting them into a tagged data model. It combines clustering and classification, rule matching, and statistical baseline comparison to perform risk determination and identify anomalous deviations for entities.
A0029.limitation: Profiling relies on historical behavior baselines; cold-start users or low-activity entities lack enough samples and are prone to misjudgment. Illicit actors can pollute the baseline via account farming that mimics normal behavior, sharing device pools to spread risk, or randomizing operation time windows to dilute anomalies. Once the tag system leaks, attackers can craft disguised features that fit the profile to evade detection. Cross-platform data stitching is constrained by data silos and privacy compliance, making a global view hard, and the large-scale personal dataset accumulated by profiling itself poses data-leak and privacy-compliance risks.

A0029-001.title: User Profiling
A0029-001.definition: Labeling users and describing them through various tags.
A0029-001.description: User profiling refers to labeled user models abstracted from user attributes, preferences, lifestyle habits, and behavior. In plain terms, it means assigning tags to users — tags are highly refined characteristic identifiers derived from analyzing user information. Through labeling, users can be described using highly summarized, easy-to-understand characteristics, making it easier for people to understand users and for computers to process them.
A0029-001.limitation: Data quality issues: user profiling requires large amounts of data; if data quality is poor, it will affect profile accuracy. Data privacy issues: user profiling requires collecting large amounts of user data; if not handled properly, it will involve user privacy concerns. Timeliness issues: user profiling is based on historical data analysis and prediction; if the data is outdated or inaccurate, it will affect the timeliness of the profile.

A0029-002.title: IP Profiling
A0029-002.definition: Analyzing the behavior and characteristics of an IP address and associating it with various labels and attributes to form a comprehensive understanding of that IP address.
A0029-002.description: IP profiling refers to associating an IP address with various tags and attributes by analyzing its behavior and characteristics, thereby forming a comprehensive understanding of that IP address. It can include aspects such as the IP's geographic location, affiliated ISP, network quality, and user profiling, and can be used to determine whether the IP address poses a risk or is malicious. In the cybersecurity domain, IP profiling is an important technical approach that helps enterprises better understand threats and anomalous behaviors in the network, improving network security protection capabilities. Through IP profiling, enterprises can quickly locate and handle malicious attacks, fraudulent activities, and other cybersecurity incidents, safeguarding business security and data security.
A0029-002.limitation: Malicious actors can bypass IP profiling blocks by leveraging residential proxy pools and frequent ADSL dial-up IP rotation. The massive dilution of addresses after IPv6 adoption also makes profiling baselines difficult to maintain. Meanwhile, legitimate users sharing NAT egress IPs are prone to false positives and false blocks, and mobile carrier egress IPs are difficult to directly blacklist.

A0029-003.title: Device Profiling
A0029-003.definition: Labeling devices and describing them through various tags.
A0029-003.description: Device profiling labels devices by abstracting device attributes, device fingerprints, operating environments, and behavioral characteristics into a tag-based device model. It performs risk assessment and anomaly deviation identification through rule matching, cluster classification, and statistical baseline comparison, serving as an extension of device fingerprinting (A0021).
A0029-003.limitation: Device profiling is an extension of device fingerprinting (A0021). If the device fingerprint is inaccurate, the device profile will also be affected. Additionally, the accuracy of device profiling is influenced by the device profiling algorithm.
